title: Control plane DB: consolidate tenant indexes and remove legacy columns
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Several control-plane queries that power the Console routes and rollout logic are experiencing periodic 99th-percentile spikes due to inefficient plans and legacy columns. We have multiple single-column indexes on tenant_id + updated_at on high-cardinality tables and an old 'env' column that is no longer populated but still causes sequential scans in some JOIN paths. Goal: reduce query p95/p99 for the affected APIs, remove unused columns that complicate ORMs and migrations, and consolidate indexing strategies (multi-column + partial indexes) to reduce index bloat and improve write throughput.
acceptance_criteria: Affected API endpoints p95 reduced by >=30% and p99 reduced by >=20% in staging compared to baseline (see metrics link)
No full-table sequential scans observed in production queries for the six identified slow plans (pg_stat_statements verified) after rollout
Migration scripts run successfully in a rolling fashion without >2% write latency regression in dedicated clusters
All removed legacy columns are dropped and referenced code paths are removed or migrated; ORMs and schema docs updated
Index maintenance cost (estimated index size across primary control-plane DB) reduced by >=18%
Runbook updated and smoke tests added to CI verifying the core JOINs and tenant filtering behavior
tasks: Inventory slow queries and map to tables/columns (ENG-logs ticket created in Confluence)
Design consolidated index strategy: multi-column + partial indexes for hot routes, remove duplicate single-column indexes
Add feature-flagged migration scripts that create new indexes concurrently and backfill partial indexes
Deploy index creation to staging, run perf tests and PGEXPLAIN analysis
Stage migration to canary production cluster during low traffic window (per migration plan)
Run deprecation sweep: update ORM models, remove references to 'env' and other legacy columns
Drop legacy columns using safe, chunked migrations with validation hooks
Add regression tests to schema-migration CI job and update schema docs
Monitor post-deploy metrics and roll forward or rollback if SLOs break
migration_plan: Phase 0 (staging): create new multi-column indexes concurrently. Example: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY ix_runs_tenant_state_updated ON runs (tenant_id, state, updated_at DESC) WHERE state IN ('running','pending');
Phase 1 (staging perf): run pg_stat_statements and EXPLAIN ANALYZE for the 6 slow queries, compare plans and latency; adjust partial predicates as needed
Phase 2 (canary prod): create indexes concurrently on a single canary shard/region during a scheduled low-traffic window; enable additional query logging
Phase 3 (rollout): after 24h of stable metrics, update application code to prefer new indexed paths (ORM hints / explicit WHERE clauses), then schedule chunked column drop
Phase 4 (cleanup): run chunked ALTER TABLE DROP COLUMN for legacy fields (chunk size tuned by write rate), validate with checksum queries between old and new views
All index creation and column drops use CONCURRENTLY or chunked updates to avoid locks; migration scripts are idempotent and log progress to migrations.jobs table
rollback_plan: If p95/p99 regress by more than 10% or write latency increases >2% in canary, revert by: 1) removing application code changes that target new indexed paths (feature flag off), 2) drop newly created indexes (CONCURRENTLY) and re-create previous indexes if needed, 3) pause any pending DROP COLUMN jobs. PRs include explicit rollback scripts and operator checklist.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Concurrent index creation can increase IO and CPU on primary. Mitigation: run on low-traffic windows, throttle autovacuum and use canary shard first
Risk: Dropping columns may break older integrated services. Mitigation: add schema compatibility layer, maintain columns for 2 release cycles and use feature flags for code path migration
Risk: Partial index predicates might be too narrow or too broad. Mitigation: iterate in staging with representative datasets and refine with pg_stat_statements
Risk: Rollback complexity if large indexes are dropped. Mitigation: keep DROP operations in separate controlled jobs with pre-checks and keep snapshots/backups prior to destructive steps
metrics_to_monitor: pg_stat_statements: mean_time and calls for identified query hashes
Index bloat / total index size (pg_indexes_size) for targeted tables
Write latency (commit time) and WAL generation rates during migrations
Error rates and application DB timeouts
Canary cluster CPU/IO and autovacuum backlog
comments: 2026-03-02 | Ava Chen: Initial triage complete. Identified 6 slow plans that correlate with tenant_id filtering and large JOINs to configs and runs. Created confluence inventory.
2026-03-05 | Luis Martinez: Prototype index on staging reduced p95 for rollout list API from 320ms to 210ms; p99 still shows occasional 800ms spikes. Investigating partial predicate refinement.

2026-03-08 | Priya Nair (DB Eng Review): Reviewed plan. Suggest adding single-row checksum queries before and after DROP COLUMN to ensure no semantics changed. Also suggested creating smaller partial indexes scoped to (state IN ...) instead of trusting updated_at ordering only.

2026-03-10 | Luis Martinez: Deployed index creation to canary shard this morning; monitoring shows CPU increase ~12% but p95 down ~35%. Will schedule broader rollout next Tue low-traffic window. Added migration PR link above.
